title: Chintz skirt (wagd)
description: A wide skirt of flowered Indian chintz. Fabrics like this came in with the Dutch East India Company and were hugely popular in the 18th-century Zaan region, where the overskirt was called a wagd.

title: New Frisian Costume by Afke Wiersma
description: Launched in 1950 as a new regional dress for Friesland, mixing old Frisian dress with Dior's New Look. This version has an embroidered linen cap and a jacket and skirt of purple wool.

title: Boy's dress
description: A woollen winter dress with pink bows, worn by a small boy. Until the late 19th century, young boys wore dresses just like girls.

title: Kotomisi ensemble (koto)
description: The koto is the dress of Creole women in Suriname, everyday wear from about 1870 and a way to send hidden messages. This is its most common form, the bigi koto.

title: Etched breastplate (borststuk)
description: Part of a ten-piece parade armour that Amsterdam's civic guard ordered from northern Italy in the 1570s. It was probably made in Brescia.

title: Mitts with a jacket (mitaines)
description: Fingerless mitts that 19th-century Zaan women wore over their forearms, in silk, wool or cotton, often edged with bobbin lace.

title: Stays with stomacher (keurslijf)
description: Stiff underwear that pressed the torso into a flat cone. The shape barely changed from the late 16th century to about 1790, and lacing it tight needed a helper.

title: Jump suit ‘Striptease Suit’
description: A windproof suit of the British Special Operations Executive, worn over normal clothes for a parachute jump. The camouflage was painted on by hand.

title: Three-piece walking dress
description: Jacket, skirt and drapery in thin beige wool with blue trim. Ties in the waistband lift the overskirt, and a crinoline gave the 1860s width.

title: Black Forest bonnet
description: Worn by married women in the Harmersbach and Kinzig valleys of the Black Forest. Unmarried women wore a cap with a wreath of glass beads instead.

title: Ensemble by Dior (John Galliano)
description: Galliano's spring/summer 2009 look for Dior, inspired by Flemish painting and by the 1947 Bar suit of the New Look.

title: Collar dress by Gijs Bakker
description: Shown in 1967 by Gijs Bakker and Emmy van Leersum, whose large, light designs blurred jewellery, clothing and art.

title: ‘Wearable object’ by Lam de Wolf
description: To wear around the neck or over the shoulder, or to hang on a wall. Its long lines refer to thread, the basis of all textile.

title: Skirt dress for a boy (rokkendracht)
description: Regional dress for a boy of about two from Rouveen near Staphorst, around 1950. Small boys wore skirts too; a silver collar button set them apart from girls.

title: The Swimming Lesson by Joyce Scott
description: Beadwork in peyote stitch from 1989. Scott uses jewellery to confront racism, sexism and violence.

title: Growth by Wiebke Pandikow
description: Plants 'grown' leaf by leaf from plastic bags: a comment on pollution and fast consumption.

title: Costume by Bas Kosters
description: Trousers and jacket after Zuiderzee fishermen's dress, from 'My Paper Crown', shown at Amsterdam Fashion Week in 2017. The fabric was block-printed in India.

title: Leopard coat by Fong Leng
description: Gold leather with leather leopards and rosettes, one of Fong Leng's best-known 1970s pieces. Mathilde Willink wore it.

title: Pliséeröckchen by Vera Siemund
description: A bridal necklace inspired by pleated Biedermeier skirts, with little bells on a gold chain.

title: Intifada dress
description: An embroidered Palestinian 'flag dress' in the colours of the Palestinian flag, made in Syria in the 1990s by Palestinian refugees as a form of protest.

title: Riding coat of Ernst Casimir
description: A wide grey wool coat with shoulder flaps, probably worn by Ernst Casimir of Nassau-Dietz at the siege of Roermond in 1632.

title: Blouse and skirt by Norine
description: A 1930s blouse and skirt from the Brussels couture house Norine, known for its avant-garde touch.

title: Dress by Iris van Herpen
description: Look 9 from Escapism (2011). Metal thread woven into silk lets the fabric be shaped like sculpture.

title: Orange sailor suit
description: A boy's sailor suit sewn in secret from orange and white cloth during the German occupation: a sign of scarce textile and of quiet defiance.

title: Wedding dress of Henriëtte van Cleeff
description: White satin with a train and beading, made for an Amsterdam wedding in 1882 by the dressmaker Lina de Goede.

title: Tunic by Paco Rabanne
description: Small metal plates linked by rings, typical of Rabanne's futuristic 1960s 'chainmail' dresses.

title: Half-mourning dress of Princess Wilhelmina
description: After her father died in 1890, the ten-year-old queen moved from full black to 'half mourning': white cotton with black motifs and edges.

title: Dress ‘Marinero #33’ by Jef Montes
description: Jacquard-woven from experimental yarns that change shape for good when exposed to the weather.

title: Silhouette by Walter Van Beirendonck
description: By one of the Antwerp designers who put Belgian avant-garde fashion on the world map from the mid-1980s.

title: Ear iron from West Friesland (oorijzer)
description: An early, rare ear iron that held a lace cap in place. Most were melted down when fashions changed.

title: Head ornament by Nicolaas van Beek
description: Sawn and bent sheet metal, a wearable object from the Space Age 1960s.

title: Uniform of a Papal Zouave
description: Worn by Catholic volunteers who defended the Papal States for Pope Pius IX in the 1860s.

title: Silk Empire dress
description: A high waist and short puffed sleeves: the Empire style that came from France in the early 19th century.

title: Stovepipe necklace by Gijs Bakker
description: Two pieces of anodised stovepipe: a 'ready-made' and a classic of Dutch jewellery design.

title: Short evening cape of Queen Wilhelmina
description: A short cape (sortie) worn over gala evening dress, together with long white gloves.

title: Filigree bracelet from Sulawesi
description: Gold filigree and granulation of great precision, probably by a goldsmith in Kendari.

title: Boat necklace (bootjesketting)
description: A gold necklace set with garnets, worn by Zaan women over the neckerchief with their regional dress.

title: Rococo necklace by Evert Nijland
description: Nijland combines materials like silver, silk, glass and porcelain, often referring to rococo and baroque art.

title: Akhnif, Amazigh cloak
description: A warm wool cloak for the Atlas Mountains, worn by Muslim and Jewish men in Morocco until the 1950s. Also called a burnous.

title: Sequinned evening dress by Mme Wiegandt-Riccard
description: Black tulle covered in celluloid sequins, glass beads and jet, with a train.

title: Volendam cap (hul)
description: The icon of Volendam's Sunday dress. Its pointed shape only took form between 1905 and 1910.

title: Robe de style ‘Le souffle’ by Jeanne Lanvin
description: A low 1920s waist with a full skirt that recalls French court dress: Lanvin's trademark.

title: Ottoman wedding dress (bindalli)
description: Velvet with gold couching. The gold and the skill in a bindalli showed the wearer's status.

title: Mourning Piece by Lucy Sarneel
description: Inspired by the square chest cloth of Marken dress, which turned black and white in mourning.

title: Hindeloopen bride
description: A bridal coat (wentke) of chintz painted with red flowers on white, with accessories in Indian checked cotton.

title: Belt by Meret Oppenheim
description: Designed by the surrealist in the 1930s and only made in 2003, from her sketches.

title: Tailcoat by J. Campbell, Latham & Co
description: A London-made tailcoat suit from 1914.

title: Punk outfit
description: Torn clothes and safety pins from Rotterdam's early-1980s punk scene, a youth revolt against the establishment.

title: Ensemble by Rich Mnisi
description: From 'Hiya Kaya', spring/summer 2021, by a South African label that retells African heritage for today.

title: Court gala uniform of the Master of the Hunt
description: Dark green, not the usual court blue. Nine embroidered branches on the chest mark his rank.

title: Volendam jacket (jak) of Neeltje Schilder
description: Printed black cotton for housework, shaped by gathering the fabric around the bust.

title: Short gala dress of Princess Juliana
description: Ordered from the Paris house Premet when Juliana came of age and took on official duties.

title: Pashtun bridal ensemble
description: Shiny fabric, mirrors and metal thread from Afghanistan, made to catch the light and every eye.

title: Brabant regional dress
description: Plain black dress of around 1900 that served for church, mourning and parties alike.

title: Habit à la française
description: An 18th-century man's suit of coat, waistcoat and breeches, embroidered with wild flowers.

title: Oranje Boven by Marion Herbst
description: By a co-founder of the 'rebellious goldsmiths', who worked early with perspex, aluminium and acrylic.

title: State coat of the sultans of Yogyakarta
description: A patchwork coat, sacred in Central Java, worn by two 19th-century sultans at court processions.

title: Silhouette by Jan-Jan Van Essche
description: Look AW23/P#11, in hand-woven checked wool by the Senegalese artist Lamine Diouf.

title: Hobble-skirt dress by Loelgen & Kriegel
description: Pink satin, silk gauze and embroidered tulle, cut narrow at the ankles.

title: Doublet of Hugo de Groot
description: Leather, long-sleeved. Tradition says the scholar wore it when he escaped Loevestein Castle in a book chest.

title: Coat by Yamuna Forzani
description: Psychedelic colour and camp from spring/summer 2018, challenging the line between menswear and womenswear.

title: Riding habit (amazone)
description: A dark blue riding habit, with elastic bands inside the skirt to hold the leg while riding.

title: Seventeenth-century men's hat
description: A yellow felt hat, found inside an old wall of Utrecht's orphanage during demolition.

title: Baby jacket with Zaan quilting
description: Thick quilted cotton with stitched patterns, warm and costly to make.

title: Bridal kimono (furisode)
description: White damask with phoenixes and a tortoiseshell pattern, all symbols of long life.

title: Beatles dress
description: A 1964 print with portraits and signatures of the four Beatles, from a weaving mill in Enschede.

title: Sweater by Loes Veenstra
description: One of 550 hand-knitted sweaters by a Rotterdam woman who knitted for decades and never wore them.

title: Maternity ensemble
description: Home-made maternity wear from the 1960s, with an adjustable skirt.

title: Ghanaian dress for I Care
description: Made in green and white, the colours of the I Care foundation, which together mean 'Go Ahead'.

title: Wedding and mourning dress
description: Black, because the bride's father had just died. Worn at a wedding in Utrecht in 1879.
maker: Mme J. de Terlinge, Robes & Costumes Utrecht

title: Chintz banyan (kamerjas)
description: A flowered dressing gown imported from India, a fashion of the 17th and 18th centuries.

title: Pink chintz jacket (jak)
description: An 18th-century jacket remade for a girl's Zaan regional dress in the 19th century.

title: Wedding costume of Isabella Stinstra
description: Striped shot silk from a Harlingen wedding in 1782, with French and English influences.

title: Felt wedding dress by Claudy Jongstra
description: Felt of Dutch wool and Japanese silk, with a waistband that recalls an obi. Designed by Arlette Muschter.

title: Gold-embroidered mules
description: Red velvet with gilt silver thread from about 1620, owned by a rich Frisian family.

title: Black evening dress
description: Beaded silk crêpe with a low waist and a short, pointed hem, made for dancing in the 1920s.

title: Innu hunting coat
description: Caribou leather, cut like an 18th-century French officer's coat, by the Innu of Quebec and Labrador.

title: Cap for Sunday-best dress (droefmuts)
description: Machine lace and folded ribbon, from the regional dress of Oldebroek.

title: Water Gold sari by Rahul Mishra
description: Hand-embroidered in gold with 3D details, from a collection about the cosmos.

title: Silk bodice (rijglijf)
description: Green silk taffeta with pink shoulder ribbons.

title: Black stage dress worn by Louisette
description: Black satin with sequinned flowers, for the singer known as the Dutch Mistinguett.

title: Cream stage dress worn by Louisette
description: Satin with gold sequins and cherries, lined in bright pink that flashed as she danced.

title: Stage costume worn by Louisette
description: A 1920s satin stage costume with sequins, drapery and a shawl.

title: National Celebration Skirt
description: The Liberation Skirt, an icon of Dutch liberation, worn at national celebrations from 1945.

title: Pearls of Makkum by Alexander van Slobbe
description: Earthenware 'pearls' made by Royal Tichelaar Makkum, in an edition of 100.
maker: Alexander van Slobbe, Koninklijke Tichelaar Makkum

title: Masquerade costume of Simon van Gijn
description: Designed by himself for the Leiden student masquerade of 1860.

title: Rajput groom
description: Red silk embroidered in gold thread (zari), worn by a groom in India.

title: Brabant work dress
description: Dark, practical clothes for farm work in early 20th-century Brabant.

title: Dress ‘8 pieces’ by Claes Iversen
description: A strapless dress from 2014, embroidered all over, partly with parts of tools.

title: Peranakan bride
description: Yellow with dragons and phoenixes, mixing a Chinese bridal costume with Indonesian design.

title: Adam's Apple by Sari Räthel
description: From 'Gender Blender', which enlarges male and female features to question gender roles.

title: Red swimsuit
description: A one-piece cotton swimsuit from the early 1900s, made for more freedom to move.

title: Sweater by Issey Miyake
description: The sculptural '3D Spike' of autumn/winter 1988/89, from Miyake's first pleating experiments.

title: Gentleman's costume for ‘Dark Lady’ by Rien Bekkers
description: From the 1999 production Dark Lady, by one of the best-known Dutch costume designers.

title: Tutu from Sleeping Beauty
description: A classical tutu of short, stiff tulle layers, for a 1968 Dutch production.

title: Bridal bodice from Marken
description: An embroidered bodice kept for Whitsun and weddings.

title: Stage costume ‘Dark Lady’ by Rien Bekkers
description: Another of Bekkers' costumes for the 1999 production Dark Lady.

title: Hat of Queen Wilhelmina
description: Worn in 1897 when the young queen acted in plays at Het Loo Palace for her mother's birthday.

title: Christening gown made from a parachute
description: Post-war fabric was scarce, so parachute silk became wedding and christening dresses.

title: Necklace by Iradj Moini
description: Costume jewellery by an Iranian-born designer who made his name in New York.

title: Wedding dress of Cornelia Agatha Vriesendorp
description: Moiré silk from 1864, when the white wedding dress caught on in upper-class circles.

title: Everyday summer dress from Marken
description: A Marken man's everyday summer clothes around 1950, from shirt to clogs and cap.

title: Dress ‘Circles’ by Stina Randestad
description: A circular design, machine-knitted from recycled textile.

title: Suit with hat
description: A women's suit of the 1910s, modern because it let women walk and move freely.

title: Child's sailor suit
description: A children's classic made popular by Queen Victoria and affordable through ready-to-wear, here from Gerzon.

title: Father's lying-in cap (kraammuts)
description: New 18th-century fathers wore a quilted cap like this to receive visitors after a birth.

title: Charm Chain by Studio Job
description: A modern take on the charm bracelet, which carries memories of people.
maker: Studio Job, Job Smeets & Nynke Tynagel

title: Double cap with crown from West Brabant
description: Pleated lace over a black undercap, for weddings and Sundays around 1900.

title: Medieval patten (trip)
description: A wooden overshoe that kept shoes out of the mud, found in an excavation in Dordrecht.

title: Stage shoes for ‘Hamlet’ by Rien Bekkers
description: From Bekkers' costumes for a 1986 Hamlet.

title: Ruff for ‘Der Fliegende Holländer’ by Lioba Winterhalder
description: A 17th-century-style ruff with pearls, worn in a 1983 production of Wagner's opera.

title: Sámi wedding clothes by Berit Oskal Eira
description: Made by the bride for herself and her husband, and worn on special days after the wedding too.

title: Wedding dress by Hirsch & Cie
description: Made to measure in 1915 by Amsterdam's grand fashion house for the elite.

title: Cocoon by Chequita Nahar
description: Inspired by the traditional jewellery of Suriname and what it means to its wearers.

title: Dress with leg-of-mutton sleeves
description: Brown silk with huge sleeves, let out for a pregnancy and taken in again.

title: Gala dress of Queen Wilhelmina
description: A Premet dress from Paris, altered for her 25th wedding anniversary in 1926.

title: Tufted dress by Jan Taminiau
description: Hand-tufted couture from 'Follies', autumn/winter 2007–2008.

title: Korean groom
description: A round-collared robe with a winged black hat, after court dress of the Joseon dynasty.

title: Urk fisherman's work suit
description: Sturdy cotton that started black and faded with washing until it was only fit for work.

title: Japanese kimono of meisen silk
description: Affordable, shiny silk with a blurred ikat-like pattern, the fashion for daily wear in 1920s–30s Japan.

title: Striped Beast by Felieke van der Leest
description: Crochet and textile in a wearable animal sculpture.

title: Patchwork ensemble by Tess van Zalinge
description: Fully upcycled demi-couture from 2020.

title: Necklace by Nel Linssen
description: Folded paper in two colours, turned into a firm structure.

title: Jumlo dress from Pakistan
description: Black cotton with rich geometric embroidery, from the mountains of Kohistan.

title: Child's outfit of Marga Groen
description: Corduroy trousers, a sweater of leftover wool and a hand-made jacket from 1970s Amsterdam.

title: Dressing-up gown (robe à l'anglaise)
description: An 18th-century silk damask wedding dress, remade around 1890 for dressing-up parties.

title: Gujarati cap
description: A child's sun cap from Kutch, embroidered with flowers and small mirrors (shisha).

title: Tabard by Alet Pilon
description: A breastplate of folded canvas that hides and reshapes the body instead of showing it.
